Groww, one of India’s leading online investment platforms, has paid ₹80.35 lakh to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to settle a series of investigations into multiple regulatory, technological, and operational lapses, following its acquisition of Indiabulls Mutual Fund. In a settlement order dated May 27, SEBI outlined a host of violations by Groww that raised concerns over investor protection, system robustness, and regulatory compliance. Among the most serious were discrepancies in client account statements. In 38 instances, SEBI found mismatches between clients’ ledger balances and their margin obligations, which were reflected inaccurately in retention statements sent to them. The probe also revealed that Groww's trading platform failed to default to the best available market price for users. Instead, the app retained prior preferences, a design that SEBI deemed could compromise investor interests. Additionally, Groww did not offer interoperability between clearing corporations—an option mandated by SEBI to ensure better execution and transparency in trades. SEBI further flagged Groww for hosting non-securities products such as UPI payments, bill payments, and lending within its trading app. The regulator warned that this could potentially lead to unintended financial liabilities for users, especially in cases of UPI-related disputes. The platform also came under fire for its inadequate risk management systems. Notably, Groww lacked any alternative or backup access system for users during app or website outages, leaving clients exposed without a way to exit positions during critical moments. The company's Business Continuity Plan (BCP), meant to address such scenarios, was being reviewed only annually instead of the mandated half-yearly schedule. Meanwhile the company has also filed drafted IPO papers with capital markets regulator SEBI through a confidential pre-filing route. The confidential pre-filing route allows a company to withhold public disclosure of details under the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP)

From celebrity-owned luxury cars to elite number plates, exotic watches and VIP mobile numbers, the app is engineered to bring trust, transparency and global auction-house standards to the Indian market. The platform’s arrival was marked by a landmark moment in Indian auction history: the successful sale of the VIP number plate DDC 0001 for an extraordinary ₹2.08 crore, making it one of the most expensive car number plates ever auctioned in the country. The winning bidder is Kiran Kolipakula, a high-net-worth individual from Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. This single transaction highlighted both the pan-India reach of the BBT Auction App and the increasing appetite for collectible assets with cultural and status value. Sellers gain access to a curated, verified audience, while buyers benefit from detailed documentation, authentication and end-to-end transaction support. Every listing on the platform is backed by BBT’s rigorous verification standards, including ownership proof, service history checks and comprehensive photo and video documentation. Beyond automobiles, the platform features some of India’s most exclusive number plates, VIP mobile numbers with rare repeating patterns and high-end timepieces such as the Hublot King Gold Skeleton Chronograph. Together, these assets reflect a broader shift in how luxury is perceived; not merely as ownership, but as a form of investment. With ambitions to become India’s equivalent of Sotheby’s or Christie’s, Big Boy Toyz envisions expanding the auction ecosystem further. In the future, the platform plans to include categories such as luxury handbags, rare collectibles and even premium real estate. For now, BBT Auction stands as a trusted, aspirational destination. Go Colors, "Comfort" Campaign Influencer Marketing Brief for WLDD From: Team Wirality (for Go Colors) Live window: 8 July to 15 August 2026 Status: Draft for WLDD Campaign theme: Life Moves In Your Comfort Zone Go Colors is known for leggings but now offers one of the widest bottom-wear ranges in the country. This campaign repositions it from a leggings-first brand to India's go-to bottom-wear destination, and redefines comfort as more than a product feature. The thought: comfort is what gives us the confidence to be ourselves and move through life with ease. The brand film follows a Tier A Bollywood celebrity in a world shaped by image and expectation, where she is being pushed into an idealised version of herself. As the pressure to conform grows, she breaks free into a more vibrant, expressive world where she can simply be herself, transforming the people and spaces around her from rigid and performative to relaxed and authentic, and moving through multiple Go Colors looks along the way. Because comfort is not where life slows down. It is where life moves. The idea, in one line An unbranded, staged style "controversy" that the internet decodes on its own, resolving into the comfort message and the film reveal. The power is in the slow reveal. The audience should feel like they discovered it. Platforms, in order of importance 1. Instagram (lead platform for the teaser, the live, the reveal and the sustain phase) 2. Twitter (X) (secondary, for real-time conversation, memes and PR pickup) Timeline 1: Teaser to film (8 to 16 July 2026) Date Day Beat Influencer role 8 Jul Wed Digital fake OOH drops. A Tier A Bollywood celebrity's gown “leaks” and reads as a style misfire, and fashion pages start reacting. Female comedians post a preview of the IG Live. Seed the faux pas. Fashion pages and comedians tease. 9 Jul Thu Female comedians go live on the faux pas. The celebrity joins the live and drops a comment. Amplification Blast 1 follows. Hero moment (comedian live). Amplifiers recount the live for those who missed it. 10 Jul Fri PR and memers comment the same day. Amplification Blast 2, the “Comfort is calling” post. Amplifiers speculate about what the live really meant. 11 Jul Sat “Diss Comfort Kal Aana” goes live in stores and on social, with a graffiti activation in regional languages. Let the internet connect the dots. Amplifiers push people to connect the dots. 12 Jul Sun The celebrity promotional teaser drops on the brand page. Amplification pages push it. Teaser push. 13 Jul Mon PR drops. Rest. 14 Jul Tue Further PR and meme coverage. Meme pages sustain the conversation. 15 Jul Wed Brand film goes live across all platforms. Full film amplification. 16 Jul Thu Marketing press coverage. Rest. Timeline 2: Sustain phase (16 July to 15 August 2026) After the film, we keep influencers active through a second phase. It runs on a set of content concepts we have already developed and shared alongside this brief (Comfort Confessions, Fashion's Red Flags, Killing Discomfort in My Wardrobe, and The Comfort Stress Test). We are not asking WLDD to invent the ideas, we need the right creators to bring them to life. The types we need: • Relatable lifestyle and everyday creators, for the confession and wardrobe-led ideas that invite audience participation. • Fashion and styling voices with an opinionated, witty tone, for the red-flags idea. • Honest, authentic storytellers comfortable being candid on camera, for the wardrobe clear-out. • Tech, fitness and data-curious creators whose audiences enjoy challenges and duets, for the Comfort Stress Test. Where influencers sit, and how many These numbers are for the launch push (Timeline 1). Sustain-phase creators are the types listed under Timeline 2. Role What they do Number Fashion call-out pages Credibly notice the gown moment and set off the conversation 5 Female comedians (hero) Carry the IG Live the celebrity joins 3 (share a longer list with costs so we can shortlist) Amplifier influencers Recount the live, then speculate (“Comfort is calling”) 30 Meme pages Mainstream and sustain the conversation 100 Teaser and film push pages Push the celebrity teaser, the film and the sustain phase 100 Core always-on creators Work across multiple beats through both timelines 8 to 10 Indicative total: around 240 creators, with some overlap between the meme, push and core pools. Content guardrails All meme and creator content must be brand-safe. No crass, vulgar or offensive memes, and nothing that mocks the influencers, the meme pages or the celebrity. Usage rights (required on all content) • Organic: each post stays live on the creator handle for at least 60 days, with no early deletion. • Paid amplification and whitelisting: we can run creator handles as paid ads (Meta and Instagram dark posts) during the campaign and for 60 days after. • Brand repurposing: we can repost and lightly edit the content on Go Colors owned channels (Instagram, Twitter/X, YouTube, website) for 6 months, with credit. • Category exclusivity: no competing apparel or bottom-wear brands on participating creator feeds during the campaign window and for 15 days after. • Extension option: the option to extend paid or repurposing rights per creator at rates agreed upfront. What we need from WLDD 1. A phase-mapped plan across both timelines: which creators post what, and when. 2. Tiered creator lists for each role: handle, platform, followers, engagement rate, audience location and language, category fit, and a one line reason per creator. For the comedians, give a longer list with individual costs so we can shortlist to 3. Flag the core group who can work across multiple beats. 3. A content plan per creator and phase: formats, number of assets, and the messaging guardrails you will hold creators to. Keep all content brand-safe per the guardrails above. 4. Your projected delivery, with the assumptions behind it. 5. Timelines: when you can share lists, how long you need for content, and the approval windows you are building in. All creator lists and content are approved on the brand side, so plan for that turnaround. First lists are needed within 36 hours of briefing. 6. A disclosure approach that stays compliant while the teaser is unbranded. 7. A talent safety plan. The faux pas is staged. It must never read as real trolling of the celebrity, and must resolve in the celebrity's favour. 8. Commercials: your fee, creator fees and any boosting spend, plus payment terms and a single point of contact. How to respond Send a deck or a working sheet, with costs as a line item breakdown we can review. First lists are needed within 36 hours of briefing, since the campaign starts 8 July. To confirm with us Priority markets and languages, and the final response deadline. Budget Total influencer budget: ₹45L, all inclusive (creator fees, management fee and paid amplification).

Phase 1 — The Rumour We put out content saying a club is opening in Whitefield. We don't reveal it's a clubhouse. We run negative PR — residents are outraged. "How can someone open a nightclub in a residential area?" Hoardings go up. Influencers react. The internet argues. We let it breathe. Phase 2 — The Reveal We flip the narrative. This was never a nightclub. This is a branded clubhouse — one that is redefining what it means to live well. And here's what's actually inside. Deliverable Structure Deliverable 1 — No client reveal. Reliable power enabled children to study after sunset, improved access to essential services, and enhanced the quality of everyday life. column4: Tata Communications and TTSL Unlock SMB AI Opportunity with Unified Sovereign Infrastructure Or Tata Communications and TTSL Join Forces to Bring Unified AI Infrastructure to India’s SMB Sector - Unified AI stack combining strengths of both companies to expand the SMB addressable market - Making AI accessible with simplified deployment and scalable infrastructure designed for the pace and growing needs of India’s SMBs Mumbai, July 15, 2026 Tata Communications and Tata Teleservices (TTSL) today announced a strategic collaboration to accelerate AI adoption among India’s Small and Medium Businesses (SMB) through a unified AI infrastructure stack designed specifically for this segment. The partnership combines their complementary strengths to unlock a large, underserved market opportunity and expand the total addressable market (TAM) for both organisations. By bringing together Tata Communications’ cloud, AI and communications capabilities with TTSL’s extensive reach into the SMB sector, the companies are creating an integrated platform. This platform makes advanced AI solutions simpler, more accessible and easier to deploy for businesses without the complexity, cost or technical barriers typically associated with enterprise-grade technology. As a first offering under the collaboration, the companies have launched an AI-powered Voice Agent solution that allows businesses to deploy intelligent virtual assistants with dedicated fixed-line numbers. These AI agents can manage customer interactions, handle routine enquiries, schedule appointments and follow ups, process orders and provide personalised and always-on support at scale. For example, a pharmacy chain can offer every household a dedicated AI assistant for medicine refills and order management. Healthcare providers can automate appointment bookings and patient follow-ups. Manufacturers can provide personalised service support to thousands of customers simultaneously, significantly improving responsiveness while reducing operational overheads. The solution is powered by Commotion, Tata Communications’ conversational AI platform and hosted on Vayu AI Cloud, providing scalable and robust AI capabilities. The underlying voice infrastructure, ensuring high-quality, secure connectivity is powered by TTL. These AI agents securely access the data they require through a unified network fabric jointly developed by Tata Communications and TTL, ensuring reliable, secure, and efficient data connectivity. The collaboration reflects a broader ambition to democratise access to advanced digital infrastructure for India’s growth engine of more than 60 million SMBs. This integrated approach not only simplifies adoption but also enables flexible consumption models – from ready-to-use AI agents to full-stack infrastructure access – depending on customer needs. Commenting on the partnership, Ganesh Lakshminarayanan, MD & CEO, Tata Communications, said: “India’s AI opportunity will be realised not only through large enterprises, but by empowering millions of SMBs with access to world-class digital infrastructure and intelligence capabilities. By combining TTSL’s extensive SMB relationships with our cloud, AI and communications expertise, we are creating a differentiated platform that allows businesses to adopt AI with confidence, while ensuring data sovereignty, security and scalability. This is also a powerful example of how Tata Group companies can come together to expand access, create new value for customers and unlock future growth opportunities.” “India’s SMB sector represents one of the world’s largest untapped opportunities for AI-led transformation,” added Harjit Singh, MD of Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited and Tata Teleservices Limited (together TTL). "What we have built together is a sovereign AI ecosystem that businesses can consume in the way that best suits them. Customers can adopt ready-to-use AI workers, bring their own AI applications onto our infrastructure, or directly leverage underlying AI cloud and development capabilities. The objective is simple – make AI practical, accessible and scalable for every business." The partnership creates a complementary go-to-market model spanning India’s SMB ecosystem through to large enterprises and global customers. While TTSL will continue to focus on SMBs, acting as the primary channel to bring AI-led solutions to this segment, Tata Communications will maintain its focus on global enterprises and communication service providers. Together, this approach not only extends the access to AI and digital infrastructure across previously underserved customer segments, but it also expands the combined TAM by enabling deeper market penetration and unlocking new revenue streams. As AI adoption becomes a key differentiator, Tata Communications and TTSL are delivering a simplified, scalable and sovereign pathway for SMBs to participate in the digital economy by combining infrastructure, innovation, and distribution strength into a single, unified offering. The companies expect the collaboration to evolve beyond voice AI, creating a foundation for a broader portfolio of AI-powered solutions and digital services for businesses in India and, over time, global SMB markets. Campaign Brief for KOLs (Instagram & LinkedIn) Campaign Theme: OOH - 13 is Unlucky? Not anymore. Key Message: The number 13 is usually considered unlucky, but it's lucky for Pune because Max is opening its 13th store in Baner. Vibe: Fun, relatable, high energy, and trendy. Guidelines & Pointers (Keep it Simple) 1. You must have heard 13 is unlucky… but it’s not for Pune or Baner. Flipping the superstition narrative, Max uses it as a hook to launch its 13th store, making the “unlucky number” work in their favour. 2. This is how a retail brand hijacks attention with humour + honesty. Taking an age old superstitious narrative, and flip it on its back. 3. This is OOH that talks directly to you, like a person. The tone is playful, self-aware, and a little cheeky. 4. OOH works when it becomes conversation-worthy and this does spark one. These are the kind of lines people screenshot, share, and turn into memes. 5. Max understood the assignment: talk to people in their language. For OOH to work, you need crisp, short and relatable language. 6. Turning a store launch into a cultural moment. Opening a 13th store could’ve been a basic announcement. Max turned it into a creative platform with a strong POV. 7. A brand having the confidence to tease its own audience? That’s modern marketing. 8. A great example of brand tone being a competitive advantage. This isn’t safe. It’s playful. It’s memorable. That’s exactly why it works. Sample Script 13 has always had a reputation, be it horror movies, urban legends, even building floors skip it. The ‘unlucky’ number. But Max just flipped that narrative in the best way possible. Their new store in Baner is the 13th in Pune, and instead of hiding from the number, they turned it into a creative weapon. The OOH says ‘13 is unlucky’* and the asterisk delivers the punchline. Unlucky for boring wardrobes. Unlucky for repeated outfits. Unlucky for anyone stuck in yesterday’s trends. This is great marketing because it talks directly to the audience. Not abstract. Not generic. Super contextual and super scroll-stopping — even in outdoor. That’s how you launch a store in 2025, not with a banner that says ‘Now Open,’ but with a cultural insight wrapped in humour. 13 might be unlucky everywhere else… but clearly, not at Max. include somewhere that the brand has been doing multiple campaigns... and it's interesting
